irrep_families.degeneracy: one irrep of dimension 2J+1 for every J >= 0

matrices.basis: spherical: the kets |J,m> of CONVENTIONS.md section 4.1 (r^J Y_J^m, Condon-Shortley phases), m = J, J-1, ..., -J; partner mu = J - m + 1

angle_axis.relation: D(g)_{m'm} = p^[det g = -1] sqrt((J+m')! (J-m')! (J+m)! (J-m)!) sum_k a^(J+m-k) conj(a)^(J-m'-k) b^(m'-m+k) (-conj(b))^k / ((J-m'-k)! (J+m-k)! (m'-m+k)! k!), over the k for which every factorial argument is >= 0; a = cos(phi/2) + i n_z sin(phi/2), b = (n_y + i n_x) sin(phi/2), phi and the unit vector n = (n_x, n_y, n_z) the angle and axis of the rotation R = det(g) g (for the rotoreflection S_v(omega) of CONVENTIONS.md section 4.2, R = R_v(omega + pi)); p as in euler

euler.d_symbol: d^J_{m'm}(beta) = <J m'| exp(-i beta J_y) |J m> (Varshalovich, Moskalev and Khersonskii 1988, section 4.3)
euler.relation: D(g)_{m'm} = p^[det g = -1] exp(i m' alpha) d^J_{m m'}(beta) exp(i m gamma) = p^[det g = -1] (-1)^(m-m') exp(i m' alpha) d^J_{m'm}(beta) exp(i m gamma), rows m' and columns m = J, ..., -J; alpha, beta, gamma (radians) the Euler angles of the rotation R = det(g) g (CONVENTIONS.md section 4.2: R = R_z(alpha) R_y(beta) R_z(gamma), the rotation by alpha about z first); p the parity of the family (+1 for D and Dg, -1 for Du).  It is p^[det g = -1] D^J(R)^dagger, D^J(R)_{m'm} = <J m'| U(R) |J m> = exp(-i m' gamma) d^J_{m'm}(beta) exp(-i m alpha) with U(R) = exp(-i gamma J_z) exp(-i beta J_y) exp(-i alpha J_z), because the rotation R acts on the kets as U(R^-1) (CONVENTIONS.md section 4.1)

matrices.note: x is the component's angle: C(x) stands for the class of all rotations by x, about any axis; entries gives D on the representatives about z, where it is diagonal.  general_element gives D(g) of every element g from the rotation det(g) g: from its Euler angles (CONVENTIONS.md section 4.2) and the Wigner d matrices d, and from its angle and axis.  Rows and columns are ordered m = J, J-1, ..., -J, as the partners.

rules: D^(J1) (x) D^(J2) = sum_{J=|J1-J2|}^{J1+J2} D^(J), each J once: SO(3) and O(3) are simply reducible
<j1 m1 j2 m2 | J M> in the Condon-Shortley convention (Varshalovich, Moskalev and Khersonskii 1988, 8.1.1): real, zero unless M = m1 + m2, and <j1 j1 j2 J-j1 | J J> > 0
C[(i,k), mu] = <j1 m1 j2 m2 | J M> with i = j1 - m1 + 1, k = j2 - m2 + 1, mu = J - M + 1 (m descending), so the phase rule of CONVENTIONS.md 10.3 is the Condon-Shortley condition

closed form (van der Waerden, Racah; VMK 8.2.1 eq. 3): <j1 m1 j2 m2 | J M> = delta_{M,m1+m2} sqrt((2J+1) (j1+j2-J)! (j1-j2+J)! (-j1+j2+J)! / (j1+j2+J+1)!) sqrt((j1+m1)! (j1-m1)! (j2+m2)! (j2-m2)! (J+M)! (J-M)!) sum_z (-1)^z / (z! (j1+j2-J-z)! (j1-m1-z)! (j2+m2-z)! (J-j2+m1+z)! (J-j1-m2+z)!), over the z for which every factorial argument is >= 0
symmetries (VMK 8.4): <j1 m1 j2 m2|J M> = (-1)^{j1+j2-J} <j2 m2 j1 m1|J M> = (-1)^{j1+j2-J} <j1 -m1 j2 -m2|J -M>

properties: the dielectric tensor to first order in the wave vector

closed_form.parity_rule: D^(J,-(-1)^J)|G = (D^(J,(-1)^J)|G) (x) det_G: at the other parity a block keeps its kets and its label is multiplied by det_G (parity_label_map); inside a 2-D block the partner order and the sign of mu = 2 are set by rule 4 at that parity (CONVENTIONS.md section 14.1)
closed_form.structure_theorem: D^(J,p)|SO(3) = D^(J) (O(3): D^(J,p)): the 2J+1 kets |J,m> are the partners of one block, mu = J - m + 1

continuous.text: D^(J) | C_inf = A + sum_{n=1..J} (1E_n + 2E_n): |J,0> spans A, |J,m> 1E_m for m > 0 and 2E_{-m} for m < 0
D^(J) | D_inf = [A_1 if J even else A_2] + sum_{n=1..J} E_n: |J,0> spans A_1 or A_2, the pair |J,+-m> E_m

families.text: D^(J) | C_N = sum_{m=-J..J} G(q), q = m mod N; G(q) = A if q = 0, B if q = N/2, 1E_q if 0 < q < N/2, 2E_{N-q} if N/2 < q < N
D^(J) | D_N = [A_1 if J even else A_2] + sum_{m=1..J} G(q), q = m mod N; G(q) = A_1 + A_2 if q = 0, B_1 + B_2 if q = N/2, E_{min(q,N-q)} otherwise

chain.rule: the image of D^(J) is SO(3), faithfully for J >= 1 (O(3) for D^(J,-), SO(3) for D^(J,+)); Sym^v = sum over l of r^(v-l) H_l, the D^(L) of H_l by h_L(l) = m_L(l) - m_L(l-2)

symmetric.rule: Cayley-Sylvester: m_L(v) = c(vJ - L) - c(vJ - L - 1), c(k) the number of partitions of k into at most v parts of size at most 2J (the number of monomials of degree v in the partners |J, m> of weight M = vJ - k)

two_column.rule: the terms of l^n: the two-column shapes of U(2l+1) restricted to SO(3), by the counts of the determinants of each (M_L, M_S)
